literal: Clothing, wealth, food, reputation, and learning—these five will not reach a person if they take up gambling.
translation: Clothing, wealth, food, reputation, and learning—these five things will never belong to those who take up gambling.
modern: ஒருவன் சூதாட்டத்தை மேற்கொண்டால், அவனுக்கு ஆடை, செல்வம், உணவு, புகழ், கல்வி ஆகிய ஐந்துமே வந்து சேரமாட்டா.
explanation: This couplet lists five essential elements of a dignified and prosperous life: clothing (decency), wealth (security), food (sustenance), reputation (honor), and learning (wisdom). The author warns that if a person yields to the vice of gambling, represented here by the word 'āyam', they will lose all five. The word 'oḷi' is used here in the sense of reputation or luster, which is quickly ruined by the shame of gambling. Ultimately, the habit of gambling strips a person of both their material needs and their intellectual and social standing.
